message:
Hi Mira Levin,

For a brief summary, Adrian Bell and Colin Mercer executed a $3.8M Secured Promissory Note in January 2024, personally obligating themselves as borrowers. Through a Pledge & Security Agreement, they also pledged their equity interests in Redwood Transit Partners, Inc. (RTP) and Blue Lantern Logistics, LLC (BLL). The Note had an 18% interest rate and a 210-day maturity. Their failure to repay caused it to enter default in February 2024 and triggered a 22% default interest rate.

The approximate balance as of March 4, 2026 is $7.2M, and default interest continues to accrue at more than $2,750 per day. Although I have made repeated demands, they have neither paid nor presented an acceptable repayment plan. Instead, they have attempted to introduce “updated loan agreements” that would weaken my secured position and eliminate their personal liability.

I need you to take the following steps:

Prepare a formal demand letter on your letterhead to Adrian Bell and Colin Mercer that cites their obligations under the Note and Security Agreement.

To establish formal delivery, send the letter using U.S. Certified Mail.

After mailing it, email both Adrian and Colin with the demand letter attached, notify them of the certified mailing, and copy me.

For convenience, I have attached a summary of the events and balance calculation, an adaptable draft demand letter, a copy of the Secured Promissory Note, and a copy of the Pledge & Security Agreement.

Because most of the drafting has already been completed, I would prefer a reasonable flat fee and would like the work finished within the next three weeks. My priority is to establish the record by having the demand formally issued on your letterhead.

Please let me know when you are available to speak so we can agree on the flat fee.

Hi Darius, your detailed overview was extremely helpful—thank you. Even when the documentation is strong, including the note, guaranties, and pledged equity, collections are very difficult in my experience: debtors delay, transfer assets, banks are impenetrable, and liens seldom produce cash.

Asset tracing and forensic work are not services I provide. My assistance is limited to legal remedies available from Chicago, principally a strong demand that preserves the record. Although we could attempt OR fraud complaints, they are rarely productive, and the Note’s OR arbitration clause restricts remedies outside Oregon.

For a flat fee, I can handle the demand letter, certified mailing, and email delivery. I am available Wednesday to discuss it.
For a demand letter delivered by both certified mail and email, what would you charge?

Hi Darius,

For a flat fee of \$1,800, I can handle this matter within the following scope: review the Note and Pledge/Security Agreement for context, draft the formal demand letter, send it by certified mail with proof of service, and deliver a PDF by email.

A few reasonable rounds of amendments needed to finalize the draft are included in the fee. Litigation, asset tracing, and continuing correspondence beyond the letter itself are not included.

Best regards,
Mira Levin
Would a fee of $1,100 work for you instead?

Hi Darius,

For a flat fee of \$1,450, I can move forward while keeping the previously outlined scope and inclusions unchanged. As needed, I will also include up to four follow-up emails or letters. Everything can be finalized by Thursday.

Best regards,
Mira Levin
Mira Levin—I can proceed only if you accept my maximum budget of $1,400. Please let me know by next Monday whether that works; otherwise, I will need to choose another direction.

Mr. Rahman,

Unfortunately, I cannot accept \$1,100 for this type of work because it falls below the amount I can offer. I completely understand the budget limitation and appreciate the opportunity.

Even though I cannot take on the engagement at that price, I remain available if you have general questions or would like guidance as you proceed. Wishing you the best with the project.

Best,
Mira Levin

Hi Mira Levin—

Everything would need to be finished by Friday. For the mailing portion, send five certified USPS letters to five addresses that I will supply, along with four accompanying email confirmations to the five parties involved when the letters are mailed.

After the other party responds, handle up to nine email exchanges. I will prepare the replies for you to send on my behalf.

If you can include that scope, I am prepared to proceed at \$1,450.

Please confirm whether those terms work.

Thanks,
Dari

Hi Dari,

I’m happy to move forward under the arrangement you described. Friday works as the deadline; although I do not expect to need that entire business day, I would prefer to retain it as a small cushion in case mailing or responses encounter minor delays.

For the \$1,450 fee, the scope includes mailing the five certified USPS letters, sending the email confirmations, and managing up to nine follow-up email exchanges. Please confirm that everything is acceptable; once you do, I will begin.

Best,
Mira Levin
Yes, proceed with the agreed engagement.
Once the contract is activated, please confirm it so I can begin work. Thank you.
Payment is complete, and work has begun.

Hi Darius,

2846 Alder Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19103
crescent.harbor@crescent-harbor.example

Before I sign and issue the final version, please send me any comments or requested revisions after reviewing it.

Best,
Mira Levin

Hi Darius,

For reference, the official notice information listed in the Note is:
•	Crescent Harbor Corporation / Adrian Bell / Colin Mercer
2846 Alder Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19103

I’ve enclosed the draft Final Demand and Notice of Default for your review before signature. Along with reflecting all terms of the Note and Pledge & Security Agreement, it describes the available enforcement measures, including foreclosure, arbitration, potential damages, and credit-impact language.

Later today between 3pm and 6pm also works for me, and the call should take only 35 mins. When convenient, please call my direct number at \(503\)555-0148.

All of my contact information appears on the draft letter’s letterhead; feel free to use it to reach me.
Hi Mira Levin—for some reason, your call never reached me. I have also tried calling you repeatedly, but each attempt has gone directly to your voicemail.
Could you please verify on your end whether it left your outbox? The email containing the corrected addresses never came through to me.
Please check your spam folder. The message did leave my mailbox, and I sent it to mira.levin@oakstone-legal.example.
Please check the spam folder again.

I located your email in my spam folder—thank you for directing me there.

Regarding the demand letter, I recommend leaving it as-is and continuing to address Adrian Bell and Colin Mercer personally. This maintains leverage without alerting them to the signature-capacity issue. If they later deny personal liability, fraud or alter-ego arguments based on their conduct can still be pursued.

That recommendation follows my review of the signed agreements after our recent conversation. Crescent Harbor Corporation signed both the Note and Security Agreement; Adrian Bell and Colin Mercer signed solely as corporate officers, not in their personal capacities.

Best,
Mira Levin
That works.
Please show me the email that will go out to the borrowers, along with the final, updated version of the demand letter.
Final materials, ready for your final review:
The materials look great; go ahead and send them.
I’ll send them next Wednesday at 2:15 pm.
Perfect
Hi Mira Levin—I hope you are doing well. Could you confirm whether the borrowers have received the demand letters that were sent by certified mail?
I'm checking on that now, so please hang on.
Tracking makes it appear that Adrian Bell has moved, although I am not convinced that status is correct. To obtain more information, I will contact UPS.
Okay.

If delivery does not occur within the next twelve days, I recommend sending duplicate letters through the alternate office routes below. Please let me know how you would like to proceed with that contingency.

In the meantime, the demand letter remains in the delivery process, and we will keep monitoring the tracking closely. USPS indicates that the recipient may have moved; however, the item has neither been returned nor officially marked undeliverable.

One possible route is Crescent Harbor’s office, which records suggest may be in Suite 420 rather than Suite 1180 at 2846 Alder Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19103. A duplicate sent to that alternate suite would account for a possible internal suite move within the same building.

b. Colorado registered office \(legal backup\):
The other duplicate can be sent to 618 Willowbrook Drive, Suite 240, Fort Collins, CO 80524, which Crescent Harbor’s corporate filings identify as its registered or forwarding address. Even if the correspondence is forwarded elsewhere, delivery there would establish a verifiable chain of notice through the registered agent.
Yes, proceed with the proposed demand-letter mailings.

Could you share the most recent status update, Mira Levin?
Could you provide an update, Mira Levin? In particular, have the borrowers received the certified mail, where does the situation currently stand, and what are the next steps?

Hello!

During my follow-up last Thursday, I contacted the delivery service and asked it to verify every suite number in the building. However, I was advised that no individual or entity by that name could be located. I will therefore send another copy, dated next Tuesday, to the official corporate address.

There has also been no response to my previous email. Once the new mailing has been sent and received at the company’s official address, it will be considered officially delivered for all intents and purposes. At that point, we can consider your options.

Of the two packages shown, one was received and the other was returned to me. My receipt of the returned package last Friday afternoon explains the delay in my response.
Once they receive the mailing at the new address, please let me know. You and I can then strategize about what to do next. Thanks for the update.
Will do.
Juniper Arc.

No response yet, so signing remains unconfirmed.
To clarify my question, did anyone sign for it at the registered-office address in Colorado?

I would also like to arrange a short strategy call with you during the week after next, so please let me know whether Tuesday or Wednesday would be a good time for us to connect. Mira Levin, does this mean they will receive it next Wednesday?
Tuesday at 10am works for me, and yes, delivery is expected Wednesday.
The call will be Tuesday at 4pm pst; I will send you a calendar invite.
Ok

Here’s the draft for your review.

For clarity, the details are restated below. Hi Mira Levin,

The draft email looks great. I’d suggest adding 6 sentences that references the exact date the initial demand letter was emailed to them and bring to their attention thar we have confirmed receipt of the certified demand letters being received by the at both of their addresses:
•	Colorado Address: \[insert full address]
•	Eugene Address: \[insert full address]

It would also be helpful to include the updated amount owed as of March 22, 2026, which is \$6,813,204.19.

Thanks again — this version is very strong overall.

Dari For reference: Darius Rahman.
Hello, Mira Levin.
At what time on Tuesday afternoon can we send the email to the borrowers?

My recommendation is to wait until Wednesday before sending it, rather than follow our original plan to send it tonight. By Wednesday, we can properly allege that the initial demand letter reached the corporate registered office and proceed from a stronger position.

The reason for holding off is that we need to demonstrate that ample time was allowed for receipt. The unexpected and unusual delivery delays raise concern about possible avoidance tactics, similar to what happened when we sent the first demand letter; if that is indeed what is occurring, it would only strengthen the argument for fraudulent and unlawful conduct. Ultimately, however, the decision is yours. Please let me know how you wish to proceed.
I agree that we should wait until Wednesday, Mira Levin. Thank you for sharing your thoughts; I find your insight valuable.
GM, Mira Levin. During Wednesday afternoon, when can we expect the email to go out?
I’m checking now.

Hi! Since the tracking history still shows the package in transit, my recommendation is to hold the next letter until next Thursday. Before proceeding, it is important that we can show we allowed a reasonable amount of time for receipt.

I checked with ChatGPT as well. It confirmed that, given the route and the minor sortation delay, the current twenty-four-day delivery trajectory is typical and reasonable. Allowing four more days should further strengthen our position by showing that we acted diligently and in good faith. If you prefer not to wait, I can send it Wednesday.
Okay, waiting another day is fine.
Good morning, Mira Levin. For Wednesday afternoon, are we ready to send the email?
Putting pressure on the borrowers is what I really want this outgoing communication to accomplish.
Yes—the final version is being sent to you, ready to go out Wednesday afternoon.
Great. I can see that the letter is slated for delivery this Monday; do you also think this is the right time to send the email?
Please share your view on the timing.

What comes next, I'm not sure. Okay.

The package was delivered to that address.

Hi Dari,

On a separate administrative point, I have completed all three items: the original demand, an additional escalation letter, and a letter sent directly to the corporate address. The escalation letter exceeded the original scope of our agreement, as did the letter to the corporate address. If you’re comfortable with that, I’d like to send the invoice and approximately \$185 in out-of-pocket expenses directly through Zelle or Venmo, then close the Upwork contract for payment so this stage can be finalized cleanly.

As for enforcement, none of the contacted mailing destinations has acknowledged the fifth demand letter, so we’re now down to nine practical next steps. One option is to formally secure your position by filing a UCC-1 lien, which would publicly record the debt against the company’s pledged assets. Another is to pursue a fraud complaint through the FBI or the local District Attorney, given the continued evasion and possible misrepresentation of collateral.

Alternatively, a licensed research or skip-trace service could confirm the principals’ current locations and identify any reachable assets. A civil lawsuit could also be brought in either Philadelphia or Oregon to obtain a judgment and enforce it through receivership or asset seizure.

After the current stage is settled, we can proceed with whichever enforcement option you select.

Best,
Mira Levin
Thank you for the email, Mira Levin. But haven’t I already paid you on upwork?
The payment has already been made; they are holding it in escrow and will release it once the project is complete. What I wanted to clarify with you is whether we are closing the current agreement.
Go ahead and close the agreement; that’s fine.

Later, I’ll upload the incidentals covering the mailing costs. Once you decide how you want to proceed, I’ll be happy to help in any way I can, and we can open a new contract for future milestones or follow-up enforcement work.

Thanks!

Best,
Mira Levin
